      49                 :             : /// An implementation of the C++20 standard library class std::jthread based on Pthreads for use on POSIX operating
      50                 :             : /// systems.
      51                 :             : ///
      52                 :             : /// The class jthread represents a single thread of execution. It has the same general behavior as std::thread, except
      53                 :             : /// that jthread automatically rejoins on destruction, and can be cancelled/stopped in certain situations.
      54                 :             : ///
      55                 :             : /// Threads begin execution immediately upon construction of the associated thread object (pending any OS scheduling
      56                 :             : /// delays), starting at the top-level function provided as a constructor argument. The return value of the top-level
      57                 :             : /// function is ignored and if it terminates by throwing an exception, std::terminate is called. The top-level function
      58                 :             : /// may communicate its return value or an exception to the caller via std::promise or by modifying shared variables
      59                 :             : /// (which may require synchronization, see std::mutex and std::atomic)
      60                 :             : ///
      61                 :             : /// Unlike std::thread, the jthread logically holds an internal private member of type score::cpp::stop_source, which maintains
      62                 :             : /// a shared stop-state. The jthread constructor accepts a function that takes a score::cpp::stop_token as its first argument,
      63                 :             : /// which will be passed in by the jthread from its internal stop_source. This allows the function to check if stop has
      64                 :             : /// been requested during its execution, and return if it has.
      65                 :             : ///
      66                 :             : /// score::cpp::jthread objects may also be in the state that does not represent any thread (after default construction, move
      67                 :             : /// from, detach, or join), and a thread of execution may be not associated with any jthread objects (after detach).
      68                 :             : ///
      69                 :             : /// No two score::cpp::jthread objects may represent the same thread of execution; score::cpp::jthread is not CopyConstructible or
      70                 :             : /// CopyAssignable, although it is MoveConstructible and MoveAssignable.
